Chapter 4: Choosing Love as a Daily Practice
You know, love isn’t just something you feel in special moments, or when everything’s easy. It’s really more of a choice—a decision you make, again and again, even when it’s inconvenient or uncomfortable.
Most of us want to be loving, right? But life gets busy, stress piles up, and it’s all too easy to get swept up in the day-to-day grind. The real challenge is figuring out how to make love a habit—something that shows up in every conversation and every decision.
There’s a story I think about often, about a busy executive who seemed to live out of a suitcase, always flying somewhere for work. Even with his crazy schedule, he made a point to call his family every single night. Sometimes those calls were quick—maybe just a few minutes between meetings or waiting at an airport gate. But he never missed one. That consistency mattered more than the length of the call. His family knew they could count on him, no matter where he was in the world. And that’s when it really hit me—love isn’t just about big, dramatic gestures. It’s about the steady, everyday choices that build trust and connection.
Or think about the woman who volunteered at her local shelter. She didn’t have a lot of extra money or free time, but she still found ways to show up. She’d bring homemade meals, and she’d always take time to sit and listen to the residents. She learned everyone’s names, remembered their favorite foods, and treated each person with genuine respect. Over time, that shelter transformed into a place of warmth and belonging—not just for the people living there, but for anyone who walked through the doors.
Most people don’t realize just how much their actions matter. A kind word, a thoughtful gesture, or just a moment of patience—they can completely change someone’s day. But it takes intention. It’s so easy to slip into autopilot, going through the motions without really seeing the people around us. Choosing love means paying attention, looking for those chances to help, and sometimes, being willing to step outside your comfort zone.
There’s always this temptation to wait until life calms down, until you have more time or energy. But love doesn’t wait for everything to be perfect. It shows up right in the middle of the chaos, when things are messy and unpredictable. It’s a choice you make in those little moments—when you’re exhausted, frustrated, or just overwhelmed.
Practicing love every day isn’t about getting it right all the time. Nobody’s perfect. We all lose our patience or miss opportunities now and then. But what matters is that we keep trying. We keep showing up. We keep choosing love, even when it’s tough.
And over time, those choices? They don’t just change your relationships—they shape the very person you become.
